title: The RPM Dividend: Structuring Virtual Care for Rural P&L Relief
summary: Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) is no longer a clinical luxury; it is a structural countermeasure against Baumol’s Cost Disease, allowing hospitals to decouple patient oversight from expensive physical real estate.

children.text: In labor economics, 'Baumol’s Cost Disease' dictates that wages in sectors with low productivity growth (like nursing) must rise to compete with highly productive sectors. Because a nurse can only be at one bedside at a time, healthcare costs spiral. Digital Health and Telemedicine are the technological 'Solow Residual' required to break this rule.

Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) devices for CHF and COPD allow a single centralized care coordinator to monitor 150+ patients simultaneously. By keeping high-risk patients out of the Emergency Department, rural Critical Access Hospitals can preserve their limited bed capacity and avoid hiring expensive locum tenens agency staff.
